samples.summary: Resize-drag commit still reads the image coordinate through the throwing `doc.getBlock`, the exact hazard this delta hardened everywhere else
samples.evidence: This delta converts `selectImageAt`, `getSelectedImage` and `updateSelectedImage` to `doc.findBlock` because "the selection is a coordinate that can outlive its block ... `getBlock` throws on a missing id". `handleImageResizeMouseUp` holds the same kind of coordinate (`imageResizeDrag.blockId/offset`, captured at mousedown) and at packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2538 still calls `const block = doc.getBlock(blockId);` — which throws (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:187) rather than returning undefined. The very next line, `const current = block ? findImageAtOffset(block, offset) : null;` (editor.ts:2539), is a dead guard that shows the author expected the non-throwing contract. Reachable whenever the block disappears while the mouse is still down — a remote peer deleting the paragraph, or a Ctrl+Z (see the related finding on undoFn) — and the throw escapes a document-level `mouseup` listener.

samples.summary: `undoFn`/`redoFn` clear `selectedImage` but leave `imageResizeDrag` live, unlike `resetAfterDocumentReplace`/`dispose` which this delta made clear both
samples.evidence: The delta adds `selectedImage = null; imageResizeDrag = null;` to `resetAfterDocumentReplace` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3913-3914, matching `dispose` at 3931-3932) but adds only `selectedImage = null` to `undoFn` (editor.ts:2104) and `redoFn` (editor.ts:2139). A resize drag can be live across an undo: while dragging, the textarea still has focus, Ctrl+Z falls into `imageKeyHandler`'s catch-all (editor.ts:2442) which clears `selectedImage` and returns false, TextEditor then runs `undoFn`. After that, `imageResizeDrag` is still set, so render() takes the drag branch at editor.ts:1845 and paints a preview overlay for an image that is no longer selected, and the eventual mouseup at editor.ts:2515-2559 calls `docStore.snapshot()` + `doc.applyInlineStyle` against pre-undo coordinates (or throws at editor.ts:2538). The fix belongs on the new code: clear `imageResizeDrag` (and detach its listeners) in `undoFn`/`redoFn` too.

samples.summary: `resetAfterDocumentReplace` nulls `imageResizeDrag` without detaching the document mousemove/mouseup listeners or resetting the canvas cursor
samples.evidence: The new `imageResizeDrag = null;` at packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3914 breaks the invariant that the drag state and the listeners installed at editor.ts:2614-2615 are torn down together. `handleImageResizeMouseUp` early-returns at editor.ts:2516 (`if (!imageResizeDrag) return;`) *before* its own `document.removeEventListener` calls at 2522-2523, so a document replace during a drag leaves both document-level listeners attached (and `canvas.style.cursor` stuck on the resize cursor) until `dispose()` at editor.ts:3941-3942. Harmless behaviourally today because both handlers bail on a null drag, but it is a listener leak the same function is otherwise careful about.

verdict.reason: Code is exactly as claimed. `Doc.getBlock` throws on a missing id (document.ts:187) while `findBlock` returns undefined (document.ts:193). `handleImageResizeMouseUp` reads a mousedown-captured coordinate through the throwing `doc.getBlock(blockId)` at editor.ts:2538, and the following `block ? ... : null` at editor.ts:2539 is a dead guard that documents the author's expectation of the non-throwing contract, so the intended "block vanished" bail-out at 2540-2543 is unreachable. Sibling coordinate reads were converted to `findBlock` for precisely this hazard (editor.ts:2313, 2336 with an explicit "`findBlock`, not `getBlock`: the latter throws" comment, plus 3799/3812/3826), leaving this site out of step. No guard prevents reaching it: `imageResizeDrag` is cleared only in `resetAfterDocumentReplace` (editor.ts:3914) and `dispose` (editor.ts:3932); `undoFn`/`redoFn` clear `selectedImage` only (editor.ts:2104, 2139) and leave an in-flight drag armed, so an undo or remote deletion of the block mid-drag lands on line 2538 with a stale id and throws out of the document-level `mouseup` listener added at editor.ts:2615.

verdict.reason: Verified directly. `resetAfterDocumentReplace` (editor.ts:3913-3914) and `dispose` (editor.ts:3931-3932) clear both `selectedImage` and `imageResizeDrag`, but `undoFn` (editor.ts:2104) and `redoFn` (editor.ts:2139) clear only `selectedImage` and leave the drag state plus its document-level mousemove/mouseup listeners live. The path is reachable: a drag is armed at editor.ts:2603-2615 with the textarea focused (selectImageInline, editor.ts:1255-1259); a Ctrl/Cmd+Z during the drag hits TextEditor.handleKeyDown, which calls imageKeyHandler first (text-editor.ts:865); 'z' falls into the catch-all at editor.ts:2442 (clears selectedImage, returns false), and control reaches text-editor.ts:1090-1098 which calls undoAction() -> undoFn (wired at editor.ts:2263). Afterwards imageResizeDrag is still set, so render() takes the drag branch at editor.ts:1845-1846 and handleImageResizeMouseMove (editor.ts:2486-2512) keeps mutating the preview; the eventual handleImageResizeMouseUp (editor.ts:2515-2559) calls docStore.snapshot() + doc.applyInlineStyle with the pre-undo blockId/offset, and doc.getBlock at editor.ts:2538 throws when the block no longer exists (Doc.getBlock throws by contract, model/document.ts:171-190; the following `block ? ... : null` ternary is dead defence). No guard elsewhere aborts the drag on undo — editor.ts:2788 only suppresses cursor styling. Real, reachable, and in-lane (sibling entry points not honouring the teardown contract, mechanism crossing text-editor.ts into editor.ts); severity major.

finding.summary: Toolbar Undo/Redo bypass the new "mutation clears the image selection" invariant. `undoFn` (editor.ts:2090) and `redoFn` (editor.ts:2122) call `docStore.undo()` + `doc.refresh()` and never touch `selectedImage`. The keyboard path is safe only by accident — ⌘Z reaches `imageKeyHandler`'s catch-all, which clears the selection — but the toolbar buttons call `EditorAPI.undo()/redo()` directly and skip it entirely. After a toolbar undo that shifts offsets, `selectedImage` names whatever inline slid into that slot; the new `imageSelectionProvider` only re-validates that *an* image is at the offset, so ⌘C copies the wrong image and cut/Delete (`deleteSelectedImageInline`) removes the wrong image. `render()` (editor.ts:1900) will also draw the selection overlay around it.
finding.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:272 `const handleUndo = useCallback(() => editor?.undo(), [editor]);` (and :273 for redo) — reaches editor.ts:2090/2122, neither of which calls `clearImageSelectionForMutation()`. Fix belongs in the new code: add the clear to `undoFn`/`redoFn`.

verdict.reason: The finding's central factual claim — that undoFn/redoFn "never touch selectedImage" — is false in this repository. undoFn (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2096) sets `selectedImage = null` at line 2104, before docStore.undo()/doc.refresh(), with a comment explicitly naming the toolbar path ("the toolbar's Undo button calls this directly, so the clear has to live here too"). redoFn (editor.ts:2135) does the same at line 2139. They assign directly rather than calling clearImageSelectionForMutation() deliberately, because that helper renders immediately (editor.ts:1288-1292) and an early render would paint the pre-undo document; both functions render once at the end (line 2132). The helper's doc comment documents this exemption (editor.ts:1277-1280: "Three entry points drop selectedImage directly instead of calling this ... undoFn, redoFn and resetAfterDocumentReplace"). The reviewer's cited caller does exist (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:272-273, wired to buttons at 614/623, reaching editor.ts:3031-3032 `undo: undoFn, redo: redoFn`), but the destination already upholds the invariant — so no stale selectedImage survives a toolbar undo/redo, and the claimed wrong-image copy/cut/delete and stray overlay cannot occur. The proposed fix is already implemented.
